Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure and canonical ordinary Lebesgue volume; dimension zero is allowed and all approved ambient section instances are part of the contract. Let v,F:E->R, G:E->E and K:Set E. Assume K is compact and each of tsupport(v), tsupport(F), tsupport(G) is contained in K. Assume actual MemLp v 2 volume, MemLp F 2 volume and MemLp G 2 volume; these include volume-a.e. strong measurability and finite L2 norm.
Assume that for every real C1 compactly supported psi:E->R and every a:E, both x->psi(x)*<G(x),a>_E and x->v(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) are volume-integrable and
  integral psi(x)*<G(x),a>_E dx = - integral v(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx.
Assume also that for every real C2 compactly supported psi:E->R, both x->v(x)*Delta(psi)(x) and x->F(x)*psi(x) are volume-integrable and
  integral v(x)*Delta(psi)(x) dx = integral F(x)*psi(x) dx.
The test Laplacian is the actual finite-basis trace. No pointwise classical derivatives of v or G or F, Sobolev certificate, core theorem, or sequence certificate are premises.
Then there exist a compact set Kprime in E and one sequence phi:N->SchwartzMap E R such that, for every n, tsupport(phi_n) is contained in Kprime, and the actual scalar quotient classes (phi_n).toLp 2 volume converge as n tends to infinity to hv2.toLp(v) in the norm topology of scalar L2(volume). There further exists a family hphiG of actual MemLp witnesses, one for each n, for gradient(phi_n):E->E at exponent 2 with respect to volume, such that the same sequence's actual vector quotient classes (hphiG_n).toLp(gradient(phi_n)) converge in vector L2(volume) norm to hG2.toLp(G), and the same sequence's scalar quotient classes (Delta(phi_n)).toLp 2 volume converge in scalar L2(volume) norm to hF2.toLp(F).
All three limits are Filter.Tendsto atTop (nhds the displayed actual quotient target). The MemLp.toLp targets are volume-a.e. linked to the original pointwise inputs. The Schwartz functions are genuine smooth rapidly decreasing real functions on real E, and their classical gradients and Laplacians are actual operators on these smooth approximants. This is one common compact Kprime and one sequence for all n and for all three limits, not three separate sequences or moving n-dependent support sets. There is no containment relation asserted between Kprime and K, no rate, no pointwise convergence, no support equality for chosen quotient representatives, and no weighted-domain/core or further inequality/composition conclusion.

Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace instances and canonical ordinary Lebesgue volume; dimension zero is allowed. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta:NNReal and eta:R. Assume alpha cast to R is strictly positive, alpha<=beta, V is C2, and for all x,a in E,
  alpha*||a||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x a) a <= beta*||a||^2.
Assume eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. Define actual measures and potential
  mu=volume.tilted(x->-V(x)),
  J=map((x,g)->(x,x+sqrt(eta)*g),mu.prod(stdGaussian E)),
  W_y(z)=V((y+z)/2)+||z-y||^2/(8*eta).
The normalized tilt is exp(-V)/integral exp(-V) times volume, and the Gaussian, independent product and pushforward are actual standard Hilbert Gaussian, product and map.
There exist kernels R,S:E->Measure E with all the following properties: both are Markov kernels; R is a true conditional kernel disintegrating J.map Prod.swap; and for every y, S(y)=(R(y)).map(x->2*x-y).
For every y in E, S(y)=volume.tilted(z->-W_y(z)), W_y is C2, exp(-W_y) is volume-integrable, and its volume integral is strictly positive. For this y there exists a real-linear partial operator D:L2(S(y);R)->L2(S(y);E) with dense domain in the scalar L2 space, D closable and D.closure closed. Its graph is exactly characterized as follows: for every scalar L2 class a and vector L2 class H, (a,H) belongs to graph(D) iff there exists a smooth compactly supported real function q:E->R with a=q S(y)-almost everywhere and H=gradient(q) S(y)-almost everywhere.
For this same D, for every real epsilon>0 and every f in L2(S(y);R), there exists u in D.closure.domain satisfying all the following simultaneous conclusions. Let u_rep and f_rep be the standard measurable representatives of the actual scalar quotient classes and G_rep the standard vector L2 representative of G=D.closure(u). Abbreviate the exact displayed scalar expression by
  r(x)=epsilon*u_rep(x)+<gradient(W_y)(x),G_rep(x)>_E-f_rep(x).
(a) For every z in D.closure.domain,
  epsilon*<u,z>_{L2(S(y);R)}+<D.closure(u),D.closure(z)>_{L2(S(y);E)}=<f,z>_{L2(S(y);R)}.
(b) u_rep and G_rep are locally integrable with respect to ordinary Lebesgue volume.
(c) For every real C1 compactly supported psi and direction a in E, both x->psi(x)*<G_rep(x),a>_E and x->u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) are volume-integrable and
  integral psi(x)*<G_rep(x),a>_E dx = - integral u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx.
(d) x->||r(x)||^2, with scalar real norm, is locally volume-integrable.
(e) For every compact K in E, u_rep,G_rep,r each satisfy actual MemLp at exponent 2 for volume.restrict K.
(f) For every real C2 compactly supported q, both x->u_rep(x)*Delta(q)(x) and x->r(x)*q(x) are volume-integrable and
  integral u_rep(x)*Delta(q)(x) dx = integral r(x)*q(x) dx.
(g) For every real C2 compactly supported chi, define the following actual functions (v_chi denotes the statement's let-defined v):
  v_chi(x)=chi(x)*u_rep(x),
  G_chi(x)=chi(x) scalar-multiplied by G_rep(x)+u_rep(x) scalar-multiplied by gradient(chi)(x),
  F_chi(x)=chi(x)*r(x)+2*<gradient(chi)(x),G_rep(x)>_E+u_rep(x)*Delta(chi)(x).
Then v_chi,G_chi,F_chi each satisfy actual global MemLp 2 volume, and their topological supports each are contained in tsupport(chi): tsupport(v_chi) subset tsupport(chi), tsupport(G_chi) subset tsupport(chi), tsupport(F_chi) subset tsupport(chi).
For every real C1 compactly supported psi and every direction a:E, both x->psi(x)*<G_chi(x),a>_E and x->v_chi(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) are volume-integrable and
  integral psi(x)*<G_chi(x),a>_E dx = - integral v_chi(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx.
For every real C2 compactly supported psi, both x->v_chi(x)*Delta(psi)(x) and x->F_chi(x)*psi(x) are volume-integrable and
  integral v_chi(x)*Delta(psi)(x) dx = integral F_chi(x)*psi(x) dx.
For this chi there exist scalar classes vL,FL in Lp R 2 volume and a vector class gradL in Lp E 2 volume with vL=v_chi volume-almost everywhere, FL=F_chi volume-almost everywhere and gradL=G_chi volume-almost everywhere. There exist a compact Kprime in E and one sequence phi:N->SchwartzMap E R such that all tsupport(phi_n) are contained in Kprime and (phi_n).toLp 2 volume tends atTop to vL in actual scalar L2(volume) norm. There further exists a family hphiG of actual MemLp 2 volume witnesses for the genuine gradients gradient(phi_n), for every n, such that (hphiG_n).toLp(gradient(phi_n)) tends atTop to gradL in vector L2(volume) norm, and (Delta(phi_n)).toLp 2 volume tends atTop to FL in scalar L2(volume) norm. These are the same sequence and common outer compact for all n and all three limits.
One R,S pair works for all y. For each y one D is chosen before all epsilon>0 and forcing f; for each epsilon,f one u and its actual output G are chosen before all cutoffs chi; for each chi its actual formula-defined localized functions are fixed before the AE-linked classes, common compact and single sequence. Kprime and sequence may depend on y,epsilon,f,u,chi and need not be common across different cutoffs. No relation Kprime containing tsupport(chi) is asserted. Conditional disintegration has its standard scope, not a claim about every conditional version on every y. All density/operator conclusions hold for every y, not merely almost every y.
All original Hilbert inner products use S(y); ordinary local integrability, weak/PDE integrals, compact restrictions, localized global L2, selected real classes and all three norm limits use volume. MemLp includes actual a.e. strong measurability and finite norm; selected class identities are volume-AE, not pointwise representative/support equalities. Derivatives and Laplacians of the smooth approximants and C1/C2 tests are actual classical operators; no pointwise total Laplacian of rough u/v_chi is asserted. The cutoff only has C2 and compact support, without range/positivity/plateau assumptions. There is no joint measurable y-dependent solution/sequence choice, weighted-domain/core certification, explicit Bessel/Sobolev conclusion, norm estimate, further functional inequality or kernel-composition assertion.
